title: Hamiltonian Spanning Tree
statementMd:
A group of $*n*$ cities is connected by a network of roads. There is an undirected road between every pair of cities, so there are ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f510f8a30b74e0050ed747bba3b931f57d778898.png) roads in total. It takes exactly $*y*$ seconds to traverse **any** single road.

A *spanning tree* is a set of roads containing exactly $*n* - 1$ roads such that it's possible to travel between any two cities using only these roads.

Some spanning tree of the initial network was chosen. For every road in this tree the time one needs to traverse this road was changed from $*y*$ to $*x*$ seconds. Note that it's not guaranteed that $*x*$ is smaller than $*y*$.

You would like to travel through all the cities using the shortest path possible. Given $*n*$, $*x*$, $*y*$ and a description of the spanning tree that was chosen, find the cost of the shortest path that starts in any city, ends in any city and visits all cities **exactly once**.

## Input

The first line of the input contains three integers $*n*$, $*x*$ and $*y*$ ($2 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000, 1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ 10^{9}$).

Each of the next $*n* - 1$ lines contains a description of a road in the spanning tree. The $*i*$-th of these lines contains two integers $*u*_{*i*}$ and $*v*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$) — indices of the cities connected by the $*i*$-th road. It is guaranteed that these roads form a spanning tree.

## Output

Print a single integer — the minimum number of seconds one needs to spend in order to visit all the cities exactly once.

## Note

In the first sample, roads of the spanning tree have cost $2$, while other roads have cost $3$. One example of an optimal path is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3a11f64ac0349d4ecd3a2b4c3443aeb7ac3b28b9.png).

In the second sample, we have the same spanning tree, but roads in the spanning tree cost 3, while other roads cost 2. One example of an optimal path is ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3fdb844c44665567f5addf82820eb6f96a060920.png).
statementZhMd:
有 $*n*$ 个城市，它们通过一个道路网络相连。每一对城市之间都有一条无向道路，因此总共有 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f510f8a30b74e0050ed747bba3b931f57d778898.png) 条道路。通过**任意一条**道路都恰好需要 $*y*$ 秒。

**生成树**是包含恰好 $*n* - 1$ 条道路的道路集合，并且仅使用这些道路就可以在任意两个城市之间通行。

从初始道路网络中选出了一棵生成树。对于这棵树中的每条道路，通过它所需的时间都从 $*y*$ 秒变为了 $*x*$ 秒。注意，$*x*$ 不一定小于 $*y*$。

你希望以尽可能短的路径经过所有城市。给定 $*n*$、$*x*$、$*y*$ 以及所选生成树的描述，请求出一条从任意城市出发、在任意城市结束，并且恰好访问每个城市一次的最短路径的代价。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含三个整数 $*n*$、$*x*$ 和 $*y*$（$2 ≤ *n* ≤ 200 000, 1 ≤ *x*, *y* ≤ 10^{9}$）。

接下来的 $*n* - 1$ 行中的每一行描述生成树中的一条道路。其中第 $*i*$ 行包含两个整数 $*u*_{*i*}$ 和 $*v*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *u*_{*i*}, *v*_{*i*} ≤ *n*$），表示由第 $*i*$ 条道路连接的城市编号。保证这些道路构成一棵生成树。

## 输出格式

输出一个整数——恰好访问所有城市一次所需的最少秒数。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，生成树中的道路代价为 $2$，而其他道路的代价为 $3$。一种最优路径示例为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3a11f64ac0349d4ecd3a2b4c3443aeb7ac3b28b9.png)。

在第二个样例中，生成树相同，但生成树中的道路代价为 $3$，而其他道路的代价为 $2$。一种最优路径示例为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/3fdb844c44665567f5addf82820eb6f96a060920.png)。
